questions.question: If an article is sold at a 150% profit, then the ratio of its cost price to its selling price will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If an article is sold at a 150% profit, then the ratio of its cost price to its selling price will be:

**Formula used:**

Profit% = ((Selling Price - Cost Price) / Cost Price) × 100

**Calculations:**

Let Cost Price (CP) = ₹100

Selling Price (SP) = CP + 150% of CP

⇒ SP = ₹100 + 150% of ₹100

⇒ SP = ₹100 + ₹150

⇒ SP = ₹250

Ratio of CP to SP = CP : SP

⇒ Ratio = ₹100 : ₹250

⇒ Ratio = 2 : 5

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: Under which Amendment, Article 75 of the Constitution of India inserted the total number of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, in the Council of Ministers shall NOT exceed fifteen percent of the total number of members of the House of the People?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Constitution (91 Amendment) Act, 2003**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Constitution (91 Amendment) Act, 2003, was enacted to limit the size of the Council of Ministers, including the Prime Minister, to 15% of the total number of members of the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
• This amendment was part of broader efforts to curb the practice of having excessively large cabinets, which were seen as inefficient and costly.
 
• Article 75 of the Indian Constitution was amended to include this provision.
 
• The 91st Amendment also included provisions to strengthen anti-defection laws by disqualifying defectors from holding ministerial positions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 75 of the Indian Constitution**

 
 
• Article 75 deals with the appointment of the Prime Minister and other ministers.
 
• The Prime Minister shall be appointed by the President, and the other ministers shall be appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• The ministers shall hold office during the pleasure of the President.
 
• The Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the House of the People (Lok Sabha).
 
 
 
• **Anti-Defection Law**
 
 
• The anti-defection law was introduced by the 52nd Amendment Act of 1985.
 
• It aims to curb political defections by members of parliament and state legislatures.
 
• Members can be disqualified if they voluntarily give up their party membership or disobey the directives of their party leadership on a vote.
 
• The 91st Amendment further tightened these provisions by making defectors ineligible for ministerial positions.
 
 
 
• **Council of Ministers**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers is headed by the Prime Minister.
 
• It includes Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State, and Deputy Ministers.
 
• The Council of Ministers aids and advises the President in the exercise of his functions.
 
• The size of the Council of Ministers was limited to promote efficiency and reduce costs.

questions.question: Who among the following pioneered binary logic and arithmetic in computer programming?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Claude Shannon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Claude Shannon is known as the "father of information theory" and made significant contributions to digital circuit design theory.
 
• In his groundbreaking 1937 master's thesis, Shannon demonstrated how Boolean algebra could be used to simplify the arrangement of switches and relays used in telephone routing and other circuits.
 
• Shannon's work laid the foundation for digital circuits and logic gates, which are fundamental to modern computing systems.
 
• His 1948 paper "A Mathematical Theory of Communication" introduced the concept of binary logic and information entropy, revolutionizing telecommunications and computer science.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Binary Logic**

 
 
• Binary logic refers to a system of mathematical logic that uses binary variables (0 and 1) and logical operations such as AND, OR, and NOT.
 
• It is the basis for digital circuits and computer algorithms.
 
• Binary logic is used in designing digital electronic systems such as computers, mobile phones, and other electronic devices.
 
 
 
• **Boolean Algebra**
 
 
• Boolean algebra is a branch of mathematics that deals with variables that have two possible values: true or false (1 or 0).
 
• It is used to analyze and simplify digital circuits.
 
• Claude Shannon applied Boolean algebra to electrical circuits, showing how it could be used to solve problems involving relay and switching circuits.
 
 
 
• **Information Theory**
 
 
• Information theory is a branch of applied mathematics and electrical engineering involving the quantification of information.
 
• It was founded by Claude Shannon in his 1948 paper, which provided a formal framework for understanding communication systems.
 
• Key concepts include entropy, which measures the uncertainty in a set of possible messages, and redundancy, which measures the amount of wasted or extra information in a message.
 
 
 
• **Digital Circuits**
 
 
• Digital circuits are electronic circuits designed to operate using digital signals (binary values).
 
• They form the foundation of modern electronic devices and systems, including computers and smartphones.
 
• Digital circuits use logic gates to perform various operations and process binary data.

questions.question: During whose reign did the Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang visit India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harshavardhana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Hiuen Tsang, also known as Xuanzang, was a famous Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar, traveler, and translator who visited India during the reign of Harshavardhana.
 
• Harshavardhana ruled North India from 606 to 647 CE and was known for his patronage of Buddhism and efforts to promote learning and culture.
 
• Hiuen Tsang spent several years in India, studying at the Nalanda University and traveling extensively to various parts of the country, documenting his observations.
 
• His writings provide valuable insights into the political, social, and religious conditions of India during Harshavardhana's reign.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Harshavardhana:**

 
 
• Harshavardhana, also known as Harsha, was an Indian emperor who ruled North India from 606 to 647 CE.
 
• He was a member of the Vardhana dynasty, and his empire extended over a large part of North and Northwestern India.
 
• Harsha is celebrated for his administrative efficiency, military prowess, and patronage of arts and learning.
 
• His court was adorned with renowned scholars like Banabhatta, who authored the Harshacharita, and the Chinese traveler Hiuen Tsang.
 
 
 
• **Hiuen Tsang (Xuanzang):**
 
 
• Hiuen Tsang was a Chinese Buddhist monk, scholar, traveler, and translator who lived during the Tang dynasty.
 
• He traveled to India in the 7th century to study Buddhism and collect sacred texts.
 
• His journey lasted for 17 years, during which he visited many Buddhist sites and centers of learning, including Nalanda University.
 
• Hiuen Tsang's travelogue, "Great Tang Records on the Western Regions," provides a detailed account of his experiences and observations in India.
 
 
 
• **Nalanda University:**
 
 
• Nalanda University was an ancient center of higher learning in the Indian state of Bihar.
 
• Established during the Gupta dynasty in the 5th century CE, it flourished as a major educational institution for over 800 years.
 
• The university attracted students and scholars from various parts of the world, including China, Korea, Japan, Tibet, Mongolia, Turkey, Sri Lanka, and Southeast Asia.
 
• Hiuen Tsang studied and taught at Nalanda University during his stay in India.

questions.question: The term 'Geography' was coined by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Eratosthenes**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Eratosthenes** was a Greek mathematician, geographer, poet, astronomer, and music theorist.
 
• He is best known for being the first person to calculate the circumference of the Earth, which he did by using the angles of the shadows cast in different locations.
 
• Eratosthenes is also known for creating the first known map of the world, incorporating parallels and meridians based on the available geographical knowledge of his time.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Father of Geography" due to his significant contributions to the field.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Geography**

 
 
• Geography is the study of places and the relationships between people and their environments. It seeks to understand the Earth's landscapes, environments, and the human societies spread across them.
 
• Geographers study both the physical properties of the Earth's surface and the human societies spread across it. They also examine how human culture interacts with the natural environment and the way that locations and places can have an impact on people.
 
• The term "Geography" comes from the Greek words "geo" (meaning "Earth") and "graphia" (meaning "writing" or "description").
 
 
 
• **Alexander Von Humboldt**
 
 
• Alexander Von Humboldt was a Prussian polymath, geographer, naturalist, and explorer. He is considered one of the founders of modern geography.
 
• He is known for his extensive explorations and scientific observations in Latin America, which were later published in his multi-volume work "Kosmos".
 
 
 
• **Ulisse Aldrovandi**
 
 
• Ulisse Aldrovandi was an Italian naturalist, the father of natural history studies. He was one of the principal founders of the botanical garden in Bologna, Italy.
 
• His work laid the groundwork for later taxonomical classification systems.
 
 
 
• **Karl Ritter**
 
 
• Karl Ritter was a German geographer, considered one of the founders of modern geography alongside Alexander Von Humboldt.
 
• He emphasized the relationship between the environment and human activities in his works.

• Final velocity v = u + at = 5 + (2.5 × 5) = 17.5 m/s.

questions.question: Since the year _______, flame of Amar Jawan Jyoti is continuously burning under the famous monument of India Gate at New Delhi.

questions.question: Find the area of a rhombus whose side measures 13 cm and one diagonal measures 24 cm.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Side of the rhombus (a) = 13 cm

One diagonal (d₁) = 24 cm

**Formula used:**

In a rhombus, the diagonals bisect each other at right angles. Let d₂ be the other diagonal.

Using Pythagoras theorem in one of the right triangles formed by the diagonals:

a² = (d₁/2)² + (d₂/2)²

Area of rhombus = (1/2) × d₁ × d₂

**Calculation:**

13² = (24/2)² + (d₂/2)²

⇒ 169 = 12² + (d₂/2)²

⇒ 169 = 144 + (d₂/2)²

⇒ 169 - 144 = (d₂/2)²

⇒ 25 = (d₂/2)²

⇒ d₂/2 = 5

⇒ d₂ = 10

Area = (1/2) × 24 × 10

⇒ Area = 120 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**
